Economic optimality is ensured through a master-of-slave (MOS) method coding technique  previously used by experts at organizations like Scada Grid Enhancing Project (CEPT) as reinforcement of different designs.  Future implications of managing inverse power flow and its importance in the development of smart grid technologies have been explored. The findings of this research are expected to contribute to the advancement of smart grid technologies by providing a comprehensive to better understand the inverse power flow problem. This paper will be of interest to experts in power engineering, control theory, and related fields working on the smart grid and renewable energy projects.

Georgia Planes Hidden Asset Pardon Amid Anti-Corruption Push  TBILISI, Georgia (BBC) - Georgia's transparency advocates are hailing a plan to introduce a hidden asset pardon as a significant step forward in the country's fight against corruption. The proposal, announced by Prime Minister Irakli Garibashvili, aims to encourage individuals to come forward and declare any undisclosed wealth without facing prosecution.  The plan, which has been welcome by Transparency International, sees individuals who disclose hidden assets facing a fine - rather than criminal charges. "The hidden asset pardon represents a bold step towards putting an end to corrupt practices that have been hidden in the shadows for too long," said Transparency International country representative, Mariam Arabuli.  The proposal has been backed by the government, which has been credited with improving Georgia's business environment and tackling corruption over the past few years. However, some critics argue that the plan could are far too lenient and that a more stringent approach should be adopted.  Critics argue that the plan could be used to pardon individuals who have evaded taxes and engaged in corrupt practices. "Georgia should not be seen as giving free passes to corrupt individuals." Said parliamentary opposition leader, Nino Izoria. "We need to see stiffer penalties and ensure that those who have abused the system are held accountable."  Despite these concerns, the government believes that the hidden asset pardon will lead to increased tax revenues and a more transparent economy. "The plan will provide a transparent and measurable way to tackle corruption and reduce the burden of unreported income." Said Garibashvili.  International organizations have been monitoring Georgia's anti-corruption efforts. And they are hopeful that the hidden asset pardon will help to bring in more taxes and reduce the prevalence of corruption. "Transparency is key to combating corruption and Georgia's efforts so far are commendable." Said Alexander Raksha, former head of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe's (OSCE) anti-corruption office.  A dedicated unit within the tax authorities will handle the disclosure process, with an expected launch by the end of the year. Meanwhile, the Georgian authorities will also establish an awareness campaign to inform the public about the pardon and the benefits of coming forward.  Once implemented, the plan is set to be rolled out across the country, with specific policies expected to be introduced for public bodies.

This comforting soup combines the natural sweetness of carrots and celery with the savory flavors of fresh spinach, herbs, and homemade broth.  **Ingredients:**  For the Broth, 1 cup diced carrots. Mr Johnson had been the subject of grueling scrutiny in recent weeks, following further controversy stemming from Russia's invasion of Ukraine. The process for selecting a new Conservative Party leader – and by extension, the next prime minister – will likely begin shortly after his departure, with a number of names already circulating as potential successors, including prominent cabinet members such as chancellor Rishi Sunak and home secretary Priti Patel. I've been following the masterful brushstrokes of Bob Ross on the PBS Arts Night aticeps program. And I must say. His soothing voice and calming presence have been balm for my soul. The way he effortlessly blended colors and textures, creating serene landscapes that transport viewers to the tranquil landscapes of the American West is nothing short of mesmerizing. His signature "happy little trees" and "happy little clouds" have become an integral part of his signature style. And I must admit that I've grown to love the way he brings a sense of joy and whimsy to his paintings.  However after spending countless hours watching his episodes on the PBS Arts Night beaming into living rooms across the country, I've noticed that his paintings have started to blend together for me. I can feel the smooth blend of his signature wet on wet technique, the subtle gradations of color and the gentle swoosh of his brush. While I appreciate the accessibility and simplicity of his techniques. Which have inspired countless beginners to take up art. I can't help but wonder what other subject matter he could explore. A Bob Ross episode on seascapes or wildlife portrayals would have been a delightful treat offering a fresh perspective on his style while still showcasing his technical prowess.  I'm not asking for radical changes or innovations; merely a bit of experimentation to keep his studio show feeling fresh and exciting for seasoned fans like myself. After all, as any artist knows. It's the thrill of discovery and creative exploration that drives innovation. I believe that Bob Ross with his soothing demeanor and prodigious talent could easily take his art in new and unexpected directions, pushing the boundaries of what's possible with a single brushstroke.  Nonetheless this is only just a minor quibble in an overall viewing experience that has left me feeling warm, fuzzy and inspired. So to all the fans of the "Old Master of Oil Painting" I say, keep on painting, Bob. The world needs more joy, serenity, and happy little trees.

Reilly, is struggling to find acceptance and belonging among the hotel's eccentric inhabitants. Arie Lev Gruzman  Arie Lev Gruzman (Hebrew, ארי לעבד גרוזמן, born July 1, 1948) is an American academic and scholar of Jewish studies. He is currently the director of the Center for Jewish Studies at Georgetown University.  Early Life and Education  Gruzman was born in Tel Aviv, Israel, to a family of Holocaust survivors. His family's experiences during the Holocaust profoundly shaped his interest in Jewish studies and its various dimensions. Gruzman received his undergraduate degree from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 1969. Where he honed his studies under prominent scholars including Shemuel Morev. He went on to earn his Ph.D. in Near Eastern Languages and Civilizations from Harvard University in 1977 under the supervision of Reuven Amitai Preor and Walter Brueggemann.  Professional Career  Following the completion of his Ph.D., Gruzman held academic positions at the University of Pennsylvania and the University of California, Berkeley, before joining the faculty at Georgetown in 1985. His scholarly engagements at Georgetown led to escalating contributions in exploring diverse spiritual doctrines at the intersections of Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. At Georgetown, he has served as the director of the Center for Jewish Studies since 1995. The institution , under which he co-founded the Georgetown Sultan Qabas University Dialogue Initiative with Sultan Qabas University in 2008.  Research Interests  Gruzman's research interests center around Jewish history, Jewish thought, and the symbiotic relationship between Judaism and Christianity. His inquiry into Jewish thought sought to peel back layers of the New Testament to explore historical events, bringing forth influences stemming from Jewish law and ethics, among other concepts. Title Semi Supervised Multi Organ Segmentation via Deep Multi Planar Co-Training  Abstract, This paper presents a novel approach for multi organ segmentation leveraging the synergy of convolutional autoencoders and 3D ResNets to tackle the challenging and debilitating task of accurately segmenting multiple organs in medical images. The proposed method, denoted as Semi Supervised Multi Organ Segmentation via Deep Multi Planar Co Training (MS DMIC), draws inspiration from the pioneering work by Richard Szeliski "Computer Vision Algorithms and Applications" showcasing its potential to improve the reliability of such algorithms in challenging environments reminiscent of the work carried out by researchers at ETH Zurich and New York University (NYU).  Most existing segmentation algorithms rely on a single modality to segment organs such as the T1/T1-cen and T2-weighted images. In contrast, the proposed MS DMIC method exploits the synergy of multiple input planes, incorporating convolutional autoencoders to extract shape features from RGB channels (capturing variations mainly related to apparent organs displacements) and 3D ResNets to convey anatomical details using a subtraction T2w/FLAIR volume. This multi planar co-training approach enables MS DMIC to handle ambiguities in annotations (partial or irrelevant) while leveraging the strengths of two modalities. As evidenced by the seminal publication of Omar Lozano, "Automatic Segmentation of Brain Tumors Using CT MRI Images," this methodology outperforms existing state-of-the art approaches and reaches human expert level segmentation accuracy.  The proposed MS DMIC method was evaluated on the open source 3D Brain tumor segmentation dataset and outperforms the MACS (Medical Image Computing and Computer Assisted Intervention grouping–validation) BCIS (Brain Tumor Image Segmentation) and MaLiMo dataset. Furthermore, the fact that simple architectural modifications to the convolutional backbone led to a performance comparable to human experts indicates the potential to address common issues in deep learning-based segmentation, such as memorization in the training process.

Abstract In their groundbreaking paper "Witness Structures and Immediate Snapshot Complexities" researchers at Microsoft Research's INCITE laboratory (Maryam Shirazi, Shwen Wei and their colleagues) introduce a novel theoretical framework for studying the intricate structures of complex systems. At the core of their work lies the concept of witness structures - a generalization of traditional simplicial complexes that enables the representation of high-dimensional combinatorial structures. Immediate snapshot complexes, a specific type of witness structure, serve as a cognitive lens to capture the nuanced structural dynamics of complex systems at a particular instant.  This paper elucidates the theoretical underpinnings and practical applications of witness structures and immediate snapshot complexes through rigorous mathematical derivations and empirical case studies. Algorithms are presented for deriving witness structures further reinforced by adaptively-framed hilbert curves.  The authors demonstrate the vitality of their approach by applying it to several prominent domains  -  the modeling of social networks and biological pathways. For instance, they employ witness structures to recount the ice storm disaster in Toronto in the winter of 1998, shedding new light on the urban migration patterns triggered by this catastrophe. Furthermore, their immediate snapshot complexes reveal novel dynamics in the contagiousness of disease outbreaks. Which has far-reaching implications for vaccination strategies and pandemic preparedness.  Ultimately this research opens up fresh avenues for interdisciplinary collaborations in this field, particularly those integrating topology with statistics and data analysis, and potentially paving the way for advance models in the areas of artificial intelligence, computational epidemiology, and control theory.

Abstract:  Title, Resource Allocation in MIMO Radar With Multiple Targets for Non-Coherent Localization  This paper investigates resource allocation strategies in Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) radar systems that utilize non-coherent localization methods to track and locate multiple targets. Building upon the foundational work of the research groups at Stanford University, led by C. W. O'Keefe, in the development of pulsed-doppler radar systems, our investigation focuses on optimizing the performance of such radar systems by allocating signal resources effectively.  The problem is formulated as an optimization problem, with the goal of minimizing the mean squared error of target localization. It is here a problem of interest to the research groups at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) who have developed advanced algorithms for signal processing in radar systems. Specifically, our work borrows from the work of researchers at SRI International, who have pioneered the development of optimization-based methods for resource allocation in communication systems.  We analyze the impact of key system parameters, including the number of transmit and receive antennas, the number of transmitted signals, and the sampling rate on the performance of the radar system. Our investigation draws inspiration from the research conducted by team members at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). Who have developed novel signal processing techniques for efficient and robust target detection in radar systems.  We propose an efficient algorithm based on the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) to solve the optimization problem. This algorithm is informed by the insights gained from the research of Enrico S. Pampaloni, a senior scientist at SRI International. Simulation results show that our proposed resource allocation scheme significantly improves the localization accuracy of the radar system compared to conventional methods.

Title including CIDI Lung Seg which is A Single Click Annotation Tool for Automatic Delineation of Lungs from CT Scans  Abstract:  The diagnosis of lung cancer often relies on the manual annotation of lungs in CT scans, a time consuming and error prone process. The results demonstrated a statistically significant high agreement between CIDI-Lung Seg and manual annotation with an overall agreement of 96.2% and a kappa statistic of 0.87. Dr. Taylor explained that the tool can speed up the annotation process by 87.2% compared to manual annotation, allowing radiologists to focus on more critical aspects of patient care. Furthermore, CIDI-Lung-Seg's results have been validated by a panel of expert radiologists at Brigham and Women's Hospital, a leading healthcare facility in Boston.  This groundbreaking tool has the potential to greatly benefit patients with lung cancer by streamlining the diagnostic process. Dr. Rodriguez observed. "CIDI-Lung-Seg has the potential to be a valuable tool for radiologists oncologists and other healthcare professionals, enabling them to make more accurate diagnoses faster. As researchers continue to refine and expand CIDI-Lung-Seg, we can expect to see a significant reduction in the time and effort required for manual annotation of lung cancer."  By minimizing the manual annotation process, CIDI-Lung-Seg can also alleviate some of the pressure on radiologists in large cancer centers like the Massachusetts General Hospital, allowing them to focus on high-stakes decision-making and innovating the most effective treatments.

Title, Uncertainty-aware Self ensembling Model for Semi-supervised 3D Left Atrium Segmentation  Abstract:  The accurate segmentation of 3D left atrium structures is extremely important in clinical settings for optimal patient care and treatment planning. However, traditional semi-supervised learning methods often rely on limited labeled data, leading to suboptimal performance and uncertainty in segmentations. To address these challenges. We present the Uncertainty aware Self ensembling Model (UA-SE). Which leverages the correlations between neighboring voxels and self ensembling strategy to enhance the representation power of semi-supervised learning for 3D left atrium segmentation.  At the Medical Image Analysis Group (MIAG) of the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ), researchers A. Tarfawi, B. GFX, and M. JITらい employed a 3D residual UNet with an uncertainty estimation module to model the spatial correlations and output the uncertainty map. The uncertainty estimation module, developed in collaboration with Dr. P. Triebitz of the Computing Infrastructure Facility of the Helmholtz Center for Health Research (SIGT), exploits the correlations between neighboring voxels to establish a reliable uncertainty map. Furthermore, the researchers proposed a self ensembling module that can model both the label and uncertainty simultaneously by considering the local graph structure, inspired by the work of the Computer Vision Group at the Technical University of Munich (TUM), led by Professor LS Haralick.  The proposed UA-SE model is trained in a semi-supervised manner, where only 20% of the labeled data is used for training. And the remaining unlabeled data are utilized to enhance the model's representation power. The performance of the UA-SE model is evaluated on the publicly available MICCAI 3D Slicer Tracking Challenge 2017 dataset. Which contains 15 subjects with segmentations of their 3D left atrium structures. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed UA SE model compared to state-of-the art semi-supervised learning methods, such as the Generalized Eigenvector Analysis (GEA) and the Discrete Low Rank Approximation (DLRA) models.  Our code and dataset are available at https, //github.com/VITA Group/UA-SE. Which enables researchers to replicate and extend our work. By addressing the challenges of semi-supervised learning for 3D left atrium segmentation, the UA-SE model offers a promising approach for improving the accuracy and reliability of clinical segmentation tasks.

Abstract The theoretical and experimental investigations conducted by research team leader Dr. Qianmei Chen at the Berkeley National Laboratory have provided novel insights into the crossover of the three-dimensional topological insulator Bi2Se3 to the two-dimensional limit. By combining cutting-edge Computational Materials Science (CMS) and experimental techniques, the team demonstrated the systemic collapse of the 3D Dirac cone of Bi2Se3 as the thickness of the material decreases, giving rise to a pair of 2D Dirac cones at the edges of the Brillouin zone.  This phenomenon exemplifies the emergence of novel topological phases characterized by topologically protected edge states on the surfaces of the 2D system. Which are remarkably robust against defects and impurities. Research assistant Dr. Rui Liu developed elaborate theoretical models to analyze the topological properties of the 2D system, collaborating with Dr. Alexandra L. Chernyshev at the University of California, Berkeley.  The experimental team, led by Dr. Qianmei Chen, effectively pushed the boundaries of Bi2Se3 thin-film materials down to the atomic scale. Their detailed study on the strained, non-standard crystals on graphite surfaces revealed the distinctive Fermi arc behavior and non-trivial topology of the 2D material. Furthermore, experiments conducted under tight control of disorder at Cambridge University has all along backed up the theoretical forecasts of novel edge-state features and preserved Fermi arc properties.  The findings presented in this paper underscore the growing potential of externally strained and imposed topological material properties, culminating in definitive systematic investigations of controlled contamination.

Nigeria Pledged to Double Cocoa Output by 2030  In a move aimed at boosting the country's economic growth and contributing to global cocoa supply, Nigeria's President Muhammadu Buhari has vowed to increase cocoa production substantially over the next decade. Addressing the COP26 climate summit in Glasgow, Scotland, the President revealed Nigeria's ambitious plan to produce 50% more cocoa beans by 2030.  The President emphasized that removing barriers to irrigation and fertiliser use would be key to this ambitious target. Currently Nigeria produces around 340,000 tonnes of cocoa annually, ranking it the world's fourth-largest cocoa producer behind Ivory Coast, Indonesia and Ghana.  To achieve this production increase, the President pledged to mobilize 50% of the country's 1.5 million hectares of cocoa land. This will involve investing in irrigation systems and fertiliser usage, respectively, to further enhance yields and support sustainable cocoa cultivation.   However, critics have raised concerns regarding the potential environmental impact of this plan. Environmental Sustainability Demand (ESD), a prominent campaign group, has expressed concerns that the government's plan to increase cocoa production may come at the cost of deforestation and habitat destruction.  _ESD's executive director, Niyi Babade, highlighted the need for the government to clarify its strategy for achieving the desired increase in cocoa production. "What is the main strategy?" he asked. "Is it to expand the land for cocoa production or is it to intensify the use of fertiliser?"   The Garden Grasslands in southern Nigeria, known for their rich soil and optimal climate are one area where the government's plans could have significant implications. These regions are already home to several endangered species  -  the endangered chimpanzee and pangolin. Deforestation in this area could compromise these species' habitats and exacerbate climate change.  Despite these concerns, experts believe that efficient management and sustainable agricultural practices can mitigate the environmental consequences of the planned expansion. Implementing initiatives  -  agroforestry, permaculture or reforestation programs could balance the need for increased cocoa production with the preservation of biodiversity and ecosystem services.  With a strong start at the COP26 climate summit, Nigeria's commitment to boosting cocoa production has the potential to contribute to the international efforts to decarbonize the global economy and address pressing issues of food security and sustainable development.

Landline users coming to grips with dwindling numbers as two thirds rely on them for basic communication.  A recent study by Ofcom reveals that nearly two-thirds of UK households rely on landlines for essential communication purposes, sparking concerns over their long-term viability as mobile phone numbers continue to rise.  For many, landlines remain a vital lifeline to family, friends and loved ones, with 78% of over-65s and 66% of those with rural dwellings relying on traditional phone lines. The UK's rural-urban divide has become a significant factor in landline usage, with rural households more likely to have a landline to cope with limited mobile reception.  In contrast Trevor Auerbach and Kate Welstead, a couple from rural Northumberland, say their landlines are "vital for communication" particularly during power outages or expensive roaming charges. "Landlines are the best option for us. As mobile reception in our area can be patchy and expensive." Trevor explained, adding that Wi-Fi dependent mobile phone services are "a nightmare".  On the other hand, mobile phone penetration in the UK continues to grow. With nearly 80% of the population now own at least one mobile phone according to recent stats from telecoms company BT. While BBしても some mobile phone contracts include landline services.  In a recent interview, BT spokesperson Anna Jenkins explained that the company has seen an "alarming decline" in landline usage despite a significant investment in retail staff and marketing. "While some consumers do not want to pay for traditional landline services. Others choose them specifically for reliability." She said.  The UK landline usage decline has significant implications for the telecoms industry. Many companies like TalkTalk and Vodafone are leaning towards digital communication services and contracts that combine broadband and mobile plans without landline, adding to the once steady decline of this traditional service, ultimately raising key questions over the long-term viability of these services.  In response to the shift in consumer behavior, telecom operators, regulators, and technology innovators will engage with decision makers to come up with more innovative alternatives that balance flexibility, convenience, affordability, and reliability.
